entities.evidence: Lot, Haran’s son and Abram’s nephew, lifts his eyes and surveys the plain.
The Jordan is the river that gives the plain its name.
The divine name identifies Yahweh as the one who destroyed Sodom and Gomorrah.
Sodom is the first of the two cities Yahweh destroyed, paired with Gomorrah as in Genesis 10:19.
Gomorrah is the second city named alongside Sodom as an object of “destroyed.”
The divine name completes the phrase “the garden of Yahweh.”
“The land of Egypt” names the country whose watered landscape resembles the Jordan plain.
Zoar marks the direction of travel along the plain. Genesis 14:2 identifies the city with Bela.

analysis.evidence: The direct object אֶת עֵינָיו means “his eyes,” so Lot lifts his eyes to look. The next verb, וַיַּרְא (“and he saw”), introduces what he saw.
analysis.morphology: The prefixed conjunction וַ introduces a Qal wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with Lot as its subject.
analysis.sense: lift the eyes to look up

analysis.evidence: In וַיִּשָּׂא לוֹט אֶת עֵינָיו, “Lot lifted his eyes,” לוֹט names Abram’s nephew as the subject. He remains the subject of וַיַּרְא, “he saw,” as he looks over the Jordan plain.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew personal name with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In וַיִּשָּׂא לוֹט אֶת עֵינָיו, “Lot lifted his eyes,” אֶת marks עֵינָיו as the direct object of וַיִּשָּׂא. The possessive suffix makes “his eyes” definite.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew direct-object particle with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: וַיִּשָּׂא לוֹט אֶת עֵינָיו means “Lot lifted his eyes.” The next verb, וַיַּרְא (“and he saw”), introduces what came into view, the whole Jordan plain.
analysis.morphology: Common noun of both genders in the dual construct, with a third-person masculine singular possessive suffix referring to Lot.
analysis.sense: sight; eyes lifted up or opened to see

analysis.evidence: Lot lifts his eyes and surveys אֶת כָּל כִּכַּר הַיַּרְדֵּן, the whole Jordan plain. The following clause כִּי כֻלָּהּ מַשְׁקֶה describes what he saw about it: the entire plain was well watered.
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וַ introduces the Qal wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with Lot as the subject.

analysis.evidence: After וַיַּרְא “he saw,” אֶת marks כָּל כִּכַּר הַיַּרְדֵּן “the whole plain of the Jordan” as the definite direct object of Lot’s seeing.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew direct-object particle with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: Lot sees אֶת כָּל כִּכַּר הַיַּרְדֵּן, “the whole Jordan plain.” The following כֻלָּהּ, “all of it,” confirms that he sees the plain in its entirety.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular construct noun governing כִּכַּר הַיַּרְדֵּן.

draft.change: Add the geographic sense of כִּכָּר under כרר and correct the occurrence gloss to “plain.”
draft.definition: The plain along a river, here the plain of the Jordan.
draft.evidence: Genesis 13:10 identifies the Jordan as the river and describes the land Lot sees along it as well watered.

analysis.evidence: Lot sees כָּל כִּכַּר הַיַּרְדֵּן, “the whole plain of the Jordan.” The following כִּי כֻלָּהּ מַשְׁקֶה describes the whole area as well watered, and the comparison with a garden confirms that Lot is surveying land.
analysis.morphology: Common noun of both genders, singular construct before הַיַּרְדֵּן. The feminine singular suffix in כֻלָּהּ refers back to the plain.
analysis.sense: A plain or district along a river.

analysis.evidence: In כִּכַּר הַיַּרְדֵּן, “the plain of the Jordan,” the river gives the plain its name. Lot sees that the whole plain is well watered.
analysis.morphology: The definite article הַ precedes the proper name and doubles its initial yod.

analysis.evidence: After וַיַּרְא, “he saw,” כִּי introduces what Lot saw about the Jordan plain: כֻלָּהּ מַשְׁקֶה, “all of it was well watered.”
analysis.morphology: Hebrew conjunction with no prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: that (what is seen, known or said)

analysis.evidence: Lot sees כָּל כִּכַּר הַיַּרְדֵּן, the whole Jordan plain. The suffix in כֻלָּהּ refers back to כִּכַּר, and כִּי כֻלָּהּ מַשְׁקֶה says that all of it was well watered.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular construct noun with a third-person feminine singular possessive suffix referring to the Jordan plain.

draft.change: Add the sense “well-watered land” to מַשְׁקֶה and include it in the noun’s gloss.
draft.evidence: In Gen.13.10 Lot surveys the whole Jordan plain and sees well-watered land comparable to Yahweh’s garden and the land of Egypt.

analysis.evidence: The feminine suffix in כֻלָּהּ refers back to כִּכַּר הַיַּרְדֵּן, the Jordan plain. Lot sees that the whole plain is מַשְׁקֶה. The comparisons with Yahweh’s garden and the land of Egypt describe a landscape abundantly supplied with water.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular common noun in the absolute state, with no prefix or suffix. It serves as the predicate of כֻלָּהּ, “the whole of it.”

analysis.evidence: יַהְוֶה is the subject of שַׁחֵת, and אֶת־סְדֹם וְאֶת־עֲמֹרָה marks its objects. The plain was well watered “before Yahweh destroyed Sodom and Gomorrah.”
analysis.morphology: The prefixed preposition לִ־ combines with פְנֵי, the plural construct of פָּנִים, a common noun of both genders. Together they form a temporal preposition governing the infinitive construct שַׁחֵת.

analysis.evidence: לִפְנֵי introduces the temporal clause “before YHWH destroyed Sodom and Gomorrah.” YHWH is the subject of שַׁחֵת, and אֶת marks each city as a direct object.
analysis.morphology: Piel infinitive construct with no prefix or suffix.
Proper noun, masculine singular, without prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: Personal name of the God of Israel

analysis.evidence: In שַׁחֵת יַהְוֶה אֶת סְדֹם, Yahweh is the subject of שַׁחֵת ‘destroy’, and אֶת marks the proper name סְדֹם ‘Sodom’ as its definite direct object. The parallel וְאֶת עֲמֹרָה marks Gomorrah as the second object.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew direct-object particle with no prefix or suffix.

draft.change: Add Genesis 14:12 as evidence for the existing sodom sense.
draft.definition: Sodom, the city where Lot lived.
draft.evidence: Genesis 14:12 identifies Sodom as Lot’s place of residence with יֹשֵׁב בִּסְדֹם.

analysis.evidence: In אֶת סְדֹם וְאֶת עֲמֹרָה, the repeated object marker אֶת identifies Sodom and Gomorrah as the two cities that YHWH destroyed.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew proper noun without a prefix or suffix.

draft.change: Add Genesis 13:10 as evidence for the existing definite-object sense of אֵת.
draft.definition: Introduces the particular person or thing a verb acts on.
draft.evidence: Genesis 13:10 places אֶת before each city that Yahweh destroyed. וְאֶת introduces the second city, Gomorrah.

analysis.evidence: In שַׁחֵת יַהְוֶה אֶת סְדֹם וְאֶת עֲמֹרָה, Yahweh destroys both cities. The conjunction adds Gomorrah to Sodom, and the repeated אֶת marks Gomorrah as the second object of שַׁחֵת.
analysis.morphology: The prefixed conjunction וְ means “and.” אֶת is the unsuffixed direct-object particle.

draft.change: Add Genesis 14:11 as an example of the existing gomorrah sense.
draft.evidence: Genesis 14:11 names Gomorrah alongside Sodom when describing the seizure of the cities’ property.

analysis.evidence: In אֶת סְדֹם וְאֶת עֲמֹרָה, the repeated object marker אֶת identifies Sodom and Gomorrah as the two cities YHWH destroyed.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew proper noun naming a city, with no attached prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: Lot sees that the whole Jordan plain is well watered. The parallel phrases כְּגַן יַהְוֶה and כְּאֶרֶץ מִצְרַיִם compare it to Yahweh’s garden and to the land of Egypt.
analysis.morphology: The comparative preposition כְּ precedes a singular construct noun of common gender. The following divine name completes the construct phrase.
Proper noun, masculine singular, without prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: Personal name of the God of Israel

analysis.evidence: In כְּאֶרֶץ מִצְרַיִם, Egypt names the territory. Lot sees that the whole Jordan plain is well watered and compares it to the land of Egypt.
analysis.morphology: The comparative preposition כְּ precedes a common noun of both genders, singular in the construct state before מִצְרַיִם.

analysis.evidence: Lot sees that the whole Jordan plain is well watered. The comparison כְּאֶרֶץ מִצְרַיִם names Egypt as the land the plain resembles.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew proper noun with no prefix or suffix. It completes the construct phrase כְּאֶרֶץ מִצְרַיִם, “like the land of Egypt.”

analysis.evidence: Carried forward: this word and its source tagging were reviewed identically at 68126:3, 68115:4, 68115:8.
analysis.morphology: Qal infinitive construct with a second-person masculine singular suffix. The suffix supplies the subject of the motion, a generic ‘you’ following the route.

draft.change: Append the place name צֹעַר to the words of צער at index 8 and update the editorial note to reflect its inclusion.
draft.definition: Zoar, the city also called Bela, to which Lot fled from Sodom.
draft.evidence: Genesis 13:10 uses Zoar as a geographical reference point. Genesis 14:2 identifies Bela with Zoar. Genesis 19:20–23 connects its name with Lot’s description of the town as מִצְעָר and records his arrival there.

analysis.evidence: בֹּאֲכָה צֹעַר means “as you come to Zoar.” The name gives a geographical reference point in Lot’s view of the watered plain. Genesis 19:20–22 identifies it as the town Lot called מִצְעָר, “a little thing.”
analysis.morphology: Hebrew proper noun naming a city, with no attached prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: Zoar, the city on the Jordan plain to which Lot fled.
